# Subtlety Rogue — what the bots run

**Recommendation (what the bots run).** Endgame build (level 60), 17/0/34 — respec at level 60. The decision loop walks 80 rules in ascending priority and executes the first whose condition is true. No party fixture places a member on this spec yet. [measured on bot runs, private 1.18.1-based realm — `knowledge/classes/rogue/subtlety/talents.yaml`, `rotation.yaml`]

**Measured in round 155** (amp-6's per-spec table). No measured numbers for this spec: it has no row in the round-155 table, which lists the 14 specs with boss-fight data [measured].

**This page is the bots' half.** It records what our party bots actually run for this spec — the level-60 build and the level-by-level order, the rule firing order the decision loop walks, the kit bands, the round-155 measurement and the recorded deviations. The hand-written guide for this spec is [subtlety.md](./subtlety.md).

## How the bots play it

On every decision tick the loop walks the rules in ascending `priority`, executes the first one whose condition is true and skips the rest of that tick. The groups below are a reading aid; the priority numbers are the real order. Level is the rule's own `level_min` — the first level it can fire.

### Single target

- **90 — Mark for Death** (`RS09-mark-for-death`) — level 40+ · intent `filler` · spell 52538
  - **When:** in combat; the target is hostile; in melee range; Mark for Death is off cooldown; exactly 2 combo points; the combo points are on the target; at least 40 energy; the target does not have Gouge.
  - **Why:** Turtle content: a Subtlety talent (165) at 40 that DependsOn Preparation, 40 energy, 180 s recoveryTime, 135 percent weapon damage, two combo points at once, and a script that puts Exploit Vulnerability on the rogue when it lands.
  - Sources: [subtlety.md § Opener (L109)](subtlety.md#opener); [subtlety.md § How to play (L25)](subtlety.md#how-to-play); [measured on bot runs, private 1.18.1-based realm — `knowledge/classes/rogue/subtlety/rotation.yaml`; supporting: `DBC Talent.dbc:165`; `sql tw_world_spell_template.sql L26995`; `DBC SpellCastTimes.dbc:1`; +4 more].

  - **Why:** 20 energy; 6 s at zero combo points and 21 at five.

## Abilities and when they are learned

The learn level is the first level the bot can have the ability: a trainer, starting, quest or item level from `kit.yaml`, or the talent point in the build above.

| Learn level | Ability | Ranks in the kit | Learned via | Used from |

- **RS01-stealth — Stealth:** This is the spec whose whole talent tree is about stealth -- Camouflage 5/5 is its first five points -- and it is also the spec that shows most clearly what OQ-1807 costs, because Ambush and Garrote, the two abilities the tree is built to improve, are behind-only at the pin and appear in no rule. The runtime refuses Stealth for every resident in a dungeon party that is not its initiate (Tick.cpp CastRefusal clause 1, `grouped_not_the_opener`), and the initiate is the tank alone (Command.cpp, Registry.cpp: `initiate = role == Tank`), so a grouped rogue is never the opener and the vocabulary has no predicate for it.
- **RS03-vanish — Vanish:** HO-TKB-PLAY-174 (PIONEER FIX, observer Hateforge playbook section 1.5, p4-group 456 core-script read L296-L339, vocabulary v35 enemies_engaged_entry): never while Har'gesh Doomcaller (60737) has a Faceless Terror (60738) alive: a Terror with no victim calls the boss EnterEvadeMode every 5 s, which resets him to full health and despawns the Terrors, and an evade by a hunter or rogue leaves the Terror victimless.
- **RS06-kick-t1 — Kick:** Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers). 193 adds the Atal'ai camp casts the boss rows lack: Heal 11642, Sleep 12098, Summon 12151 (DB, docs/research/db-queries/tkbplay-192.result.txt).
- **RS06-kick-t2 — Kick:** HO-TKB-PLAY-192 and 193 (PIONEER FIX, orchestrator, p1-loop v41 casting list): the ranked version of RS06-kick, tier 2 of 3 (rank 2, fears, charms, polymorphs, stuns and sleeps; 14 ids). Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers).
- **RS06-kick-t3 — Kick:** HO-TKB-PLAY-192 and 193 (PIONEER FIX, orchestrator, p1-loop v41 casting list): the ranked version of RS06-kick, tier 3 of 3 (rank 2, summons and interruptible channels; 14 ids). Same when and same spell; the view takes only a caster whose interruptible cast is one of the listed ids, so the kick goes to a heal, then a fear, charm, polymorph, stun or sleep, then a summon or channel, then the nearest caster (the plain rule, which keeps nukes and fillers).
- **RS06-kick — Kick:** The interrupt: 25 energy, 10 s categoryRecoveryTime, spent on a cast rather than on cooldown. A bot only interrupted the mob it had selected, so with the party on another mob nobody stopped the heal or the cast (Jammal'an's Healing Wave, the Hateforge cleric's Greater Heal).
- **RS08-gouge — Gouge:** HO-TKB-PLAY-028 (orchestrator, levelling window): Gouge is broken by any damage (AuraInterruptFlags 2, removed on damage taken) and this rule used to fire on the ONLY target and be broken by the very next push: Vessia (Assassination, level 10, solo) Gouged at hp < 30 on her one mob and Sinister Strike followed 1-4 s later, twice (stream 20.jsonl 13:41:13 and 13:42:05). HO-TKB-PLAY-029 (orchestrator, vocabulary v10): the archive uses it on a SECOND mob ("If a second mob joins, Gouge one and kill the other", "If both are on you, Gouge one, then Evasion"), and `target: other_engaged` now aims it there: the nearest living hostile attacking the rogue that is not the kill target, read through its own health, auras and melee reach.
- **RS04b-preparation-second-mark — Preparation:** Fires on a boss of the dungeon plan, with Mark on cooldown and a Shadow of Death cast within the last 30 s (`self.since_cast_ms(52710)`, state-vocabulary v36), so it is only spent right after a completed burst, never as a cooldown refill on nothing; the next tick RS09 (priority 90, two points on the target) and RS11 (five points) repeat the burst.
- **RS10-slice-and-dice — Slice and Dice:** `combo_on_target` carries the archive's other warning about the same resource -- "Do not apply a combo-point builder to an add; it wipes the boss's combo points (combo points persist per target since CC2, but only within a single target's pool)". While the target is Gouged (aura 1776) every finisher waits, as RS12's own gate does.
- **RS11-shadow-of-death — Shadow of Death:** Turtle content: a Subtlety talent (161) at 30, taken here at 31; 30 energy, 60 s recoveryTime, 6 s at every combo count -- its aura script accumulates the damage dealt to the target and detonates it when the aura ends, and the amount it can hold is set from the combo points spent.
- **RS10k-kidney-shot-runner — Kidney Shot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-095 (orchestrator rank 3, round 106): Kidney Shot (spell 408, level 30, 20 energy, a combo-point stun finisher on a 20 s cooldown) ALONE, on a fleeing mob or an elite with three or more combo points: the guide calls it the stun finisher for dangerous mobs (rogue/leveling.md L95, L167, L184). The second attacker cannot be the target (the combo points are on the main target; `target: other_engaged` would aim a finisher at a mob with none), so the rule is the runner and the elite.
- **RS13-eviscerate — Eviscerate:** 30 energy, direct damage, no duration to lose, so it is gated on the target being nearly dead rather than on an aura. The archive''s 60-level rows say 5 here; the format has no level_max, so the early rule applies at every level (OQ-2599 asks for a level predicate).
- **RS10c-garrote — Garrote:** HO-TKB-PLAY-027 (decision 86, OQ-1807): Garrote 703 is spellLevel 14, 50 energy, Stealth required, no weapon requirement, behind-only at the pin: the opener a rogue without a dagger still has from behind. A grouped rogue is refused Stealth (grouped_not_the_opener) and the Stealth rule is solo-only, so `aura_self(1784)` is true only while levelling alone: no effect in a dungeon party.
- **RS10b-ambush — Ambush:** HO-TKB-PLAY-027 (decision 86, OQ-1807): the stealth opener from behind. Ambush 8676 is spellLevel 18, 60 energy, Stealth required, behind-only at the pin.
- **RS13a-cheap-shot — Cheap Shot:** HO-TKB-PLAY-011 (decision 62, ROG-05): the solo opener from Stealth, placed directly above the first builder. At the pin Cheap Shot 1833 is spellLevel 26, 60 energy, stances 1 << 29 (Stealth required), not behind-only.
- **RS16-throw — Throw:** HO-TKB-PLAY-081 (rogue opener audit, round 94 streams, orchestrator: the stealth opener barely lands): not while Stealth is up. While the rogue walks in, the `approach` rule is skipped as `already moving` and the walk goes on to the next true rule, so Throw fired on 340 of 369 stealthed ticks with a hostile 8-30 yd away: the rogue broke its own Stealth at range (Stealth gained 3,630 and lost 3,558 in 4 hours; the target was in melee range on 99 of 15,607 stealthed ticks).

## What the bots do not do (from the rule notes)

Sentences from the rules' notes that say what is deliberately not implemented, or that name an open question.

- **RS00w-dissolvent-ii-main:** The guide's Deadly V and Corrosive II are AQ20 items and are not built; Deadly and Corrosive on bosses is contested for Combat Envenom in the guide and is not built either.
- **RS00x-dissolvent-ii-off:** The guide's Deadly V and Corrosive II are AQ20 items and are not built; Deadly and Corrosive on bosses is contested for Combat Envenom in the guide and is not built either.
- **RS04b-preparation-second-mark:** NOT built: the Vanish -> Garrote step between the two bursts and the advice to skip the second Mark on short fights (L126): no sourced trigger for a fight length.
- **RS13-eviscerate:** The archive's combat playbook gives Eviscerate the condition "5 combo points, target will die before Rupture pays off or target is bleed-immune" -- Rupture is not in this file, so Eviscerate is the spec's only dump and the second clause is always satisfied.
